Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,

  1
 closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

  8
 SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  ******  ITEM  CONTINUED  FROM  COUNCIL  MEETING  OF JANUARY  13, 2026.  ******

  SUBJECT:  REPORT  ON SOUTH  GATE'S  BTTDGET  ST ATUS  AND  THE  COMPONENTS
  REQUIRED  TO  BE  COMPLETED  TO  DESIGN  A UTILITY  USERS  TAX  MEASURE
  INCLUDING  RESOLUTIONS  DECLARING  A FISCAL  EMERGENCY  AND  CALLING
  FOR  A SPECIAL  ELECTION  ON JUNE  2, 2026

  PURPOSE:  To educate  the Community  and Council  on the current  state of the City's  budget
  and the structural  deficit  that currently  exists.  A description  of potential  budget  cuts to services
  will  be presented  and an outline  of how  a Utility  Users Tax measure  is constructed  with  a sample
  version  will  be presented.  Resolutions  have been prepared  for discussion  and possible  adoption  for
  both  the Declaration  of a Fiscal  Emergency,  and to Call  a Special  Election  on Tuesday  June 2,
  2026 to adopt an Ordinance  for a Utility  Users Tax measure,  subject  to voter  approval.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Adopting  a Resolution  declaring  a Fiscal  Emergency;
  b.  Adopting  a Resolution  calling  a Special  Election,  request  that the Los Angeles  County
  Board  of  Supervisors  ("Board  of  Supervisors")  authorize  the  Los  Angeles  County
  Registrar-Recorder  / County  Clerk  ("County  Elections  Official")  to render  all  services
  necessary  to conduct  the Election,  allow  for Ballot  Arguments,  and an Impartial  Analysis;
  and
  c.  Reviewing  the draft Ordinance  for voter  consideration  of the Utility  Users Tax.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Election  expenses  are expected  to be approximately  $258,457  and were not
  included  in the current  fiscal  budget.  Election  costs will  be funded  from  available  General  Fund
  reserves.

  NOTICING  REQUIREMENTS:  None  required.

  ANALYSIS:  The City  has been able to sustain  a Mgli  level  of community  services  and retain
  quality  City  staff and services  providers  by actively  pursuing  and recovering  "one-time"  revenues
  to fill  the City's  growing  structural  deficit.  During  this time,  revenues  within  the City's  General

  1

  10
 Fund,  sales tax,  property  tax,  and Vehicle  License  Fees remained  static  with  some  growth  in

property  tax, but  with  limited  or no growth  in the other  General  Fund  revenue  sources.  More
recently,  all Cities  are facing  a significant  downward  adjustment  to revenue  from  the current  tariff
challenges  and the downward  trend  in the economy.  South  Gate, like most  other  cities,  is being
significantly  impacted  by these trends.  The rising  costs for energy,  materials,  supplies  and services
along with  limited  growth  in revenue  have contributed  to the City's  structural  deficit,  which  is now
projected  to reach $9,000,000  for the coming  fiscal  year.

Recap  of Adopted  Budget
As reported  to the City  Council  on July  22, 2025,  the General  Fund  unassigned  balance  was
projected  to be $3,135,356 at July 1, 2025.  General  Fund revenues  are budgeted  at $70,943,552,
an amount  insufficient  to sustain  current  service  levels  without  reliance  on one-time  measures.
Expenditures  are budgeted  at $78,157,559  for fiscal year 2025-26,  resulting  in a structural  shortfall
of over $7 million.

Due to the exhaustion  of prior  one-time  federal  relief  funds;  legally  constrained  growth  in  core

revenues  under Proposition  13; softening  and volatile  sales tax receipts;  declining  interest  earnings
resulting  from  reduced  fund  balances;  and substantial,  non-discretionary  increases  in pension
contributions,  insurance  premiums,  and  inflation-driven  operating  costs,  the  City's  ongoing

expenditures  materially  exceed its recurring  revenues.

As a result,  the City is experiencing  a structural  operating  deficit  exceeding  $7 million  in FY 2025-
26, which  is being temporarily  mitigated  through  the use of reserves  and interfund  transfers.  These
measures  are non-recurring  and unsustainable.  Based  on the City's  adopted  multi-year  financial
forecast,  the General  Fund deficit  is projected  to increase  to more than $9 million  in FY 2026-27,
at which  point remaining  discretionary  reserves  will  be insufficient  to support  continued  operations
at current  service  levels.

Absent  immediate  action,  the continued  depletion  of limited  General  Fund reserves  will  impair  the
City's  ability  to maintain  essential  public  safety,  infrastructure,  and community  services,  thereby
posing  a current  and immediate  threat to the public  health,  safety,  and welfare.  Delay  in addressing
this condition  would  result  in severe budget  cuts that will  create significant  cuts to current  services
currently  offered  by the City.  If no additional  revenue  is fund  by the end of the current  25/26
Fiscal  Year,  a $9,000,000  cut to City  services  will  be required.  This  cut will  impact  all general
fund  services  including  services  provided  by  the  Police,  Parks  and  Recreation,  Community
Development,  and Public  Works  departments.

City's  Actions  to Close  the Budget  Deficit
The City  Council  and City  staff have not stood idly by knowing  that a fiscal  crisis  was coming.  To
be fiscally  responsible,  the City has done the following:
  *  Reorganized  and consolidated  Departments  to create more efficiency.
  *  Increased  fees for general  services,  and increased  sewer rates to eliminate  the general  fund
  from  subsidizing  that service.
  *  Enacted  a personnel  hiring  freeze  for non-essential  functions  and services.
  *  Reviewedstaffsalaryallocationstomaximizetheuseofwaterandspecialfundingsources.
  *  Reviewed  City  operations  for operational  and cost efficiencies.

  2

  11
 City  staff and City  Council  continue  to review  operations  and reduce  City  costs; unfortunately,  the
scope and size of the General  Fund deficit  cannot  be solved  with  cost-cutting  measures  alone.

Potential  Revenue  Enhancement  Measure  to Protect  and Maintain  Vital  Services
The General  Fund  deficit  is approximately  9.2%  of the overall  General  Fund budget,  even with
the reductions  noted  above.  To address  the $7.21  million  structural  deficit  will  require  a new
revenue  source.  Without  a strong  and reliable  revenue  source, the City  will  not be able to maintain
and improve  City  services  such as police  anti-gang  and anti-drug  programs,  neighborhood  graffiti
abatement  programs,  after school  and park and recreation  programs,  and senior  services.

As proposed,  the voters  of the City  of South  Gate will  be asked to approve  a UUT.  The revenue
raised would,  legally,  be required  to be used in the City of South Gate and could not be taken away
by the County  or the state. The revenue  collected  will  be sufficient  to eliminate  the structural  deficit
and to maintain  and improve  vital  City  services.  Without  new revenue,  the City  will  be forced  to
reduce  essential  community  services  beginning  in the next fiscal  year.

Required  Council  Actions
The City  Council  is being  presented  with  all the required  resolutions  for action.  The resolution
declaring  a fiscal  emergency  will  require  a unanimous  vote of the City  Council.  The resolution
that  calls for a special  municipal  election,  approve  the ballot  question  with  a directive  for the City
Attorney  to prepare  an impartial  analysis,  and provide  support  and opposition  arguments  and
rebuttals  for the Election  ballot  requires  a 4/5'h super majority  vote of the City  Council.

The legal deadline  to place a ballot  measure  on the June 2, 2026 election  ballot  is March  6, 2026.
A decision  now  helps to ensure that all infori'national  materials  can be disseminated  to the voters
in a timely  fashion  and that there is ample  time for the request  and collection  of absentee  ballots.

BACKGROUND:
The City's  Current  Budget  Challenge
The City  is facing  a structural  budget  deficit,  meaning  the ongoing  cost of delivering  essential,
municipal  and utility  services  is higher  than the revenue  the City receives.  This deficit  is not a one-
time issue;  it is ongoing  and long-term  and will  continue  to grow  unless  action  is taken.  Without
new, reliable  funding,  the City  will  eventually  be unable  to maintain  current  service  levels.

Why  a Utility  Users  Tax  (UUT)?
A UUT  would  provide  a stable, dedicated  general  fund revenue  source to provide  funds to pay for
City services.  All surrounding  south Los Angeles  cities have an active  Utility  Users Tax to provide
significant  general  fund revenue.  South  Gate has never had a Utility  Users Tax to provide  revenue
for general  fund services.

If a UUT  measure  was  passed in South  Gate, the budget  deficit  would  be fixed  and current  service
levels  would  be maintained.  This  funding  would  help close the structural  gap and ensure the City
can maintain  police,  parks and recreation,  community  development,  and public  works  services  for
the community.

  3

  12
 Benefits  to Residents
A UUT  helps the City  avoid  significant  service  reductions  in the future.  These  services  include
Police  911 response,  school  crossing  guards,  parks and recreation  facilities  and programs,  special
events,  plaru'iing,  building  and code enforcement  services,  and public  works  services.  The UUT
also supports  long-term  financial  stability  and responsible  management  of community  resources.

The Cost of Doing  Nothing
Without  a new revenue  source,  the City will  need to consider:
  *  Cutting  service  levels,  including  municipal  and infrastructure  services.  The presentation
  that will  be provided  outlines  the scope of the projected  budget  cuts to service  and the
  impacts  these will  have on the corni'nunity.
  *  Delaying  maintenance  or upgrades,  which  can increase  long-teri'n  costs.
  *  Using  emergency  reserves,  however,  the City  currently  has a minimum  amount  of reserves
  that meet industry  standards  for fiscal  health.  Drawing  down these reserves  any further  will
  not be sustainable  or fiscally  responsible.

Tlie  UUT  is a proactive  measure  that  allows  the City  to stabilize  its budget,  protect  essential
services, and plan responsibly  for the future.  The UUT  also provides  a funding  stream  to preserve
vital City services.

  WHEREAS,  the City  is in a financial  state of emergency,  having  experienced  a structural

  A.  Telecommunication  Services

  or its billing  agent. There  is a rebuttable  presumption  that telecommunication  services,
  which  are billed  to a billing  or service  address  in the city,  are used, in whole  or in part,

Section  7.29.060  Effect  of Comingling  Taxable  Items  with  Nontaxable  Items

If any nontaxable  charges are combined  with and not separately  stated from taxable service charges
on a customer  bill  or invoice,  the combined  charge  is subject  to tax unless the service  supplier
identifies,  by reasonable  and verifiable  standards,  the portions  of the combined  charge that are
nontaxable  and taxable through  the service  supplier's  books and records kept in the regular  course
of business,  and in accordance  with  generally  accepted accounting  principles,  and not created and
maintained  for tax purposes.  A service  supplier  has the burden to prove the proper  apportionment
of taxable  and nontaxable  charges.  If the service  supplier  offers  a combination  of taxable  and
nontaxable  services,  and the charges are separately  stated, then for taxation  purposes,  the values
assigned the taxable  and nontaxable  services  shall be based on its books  and records  kept in the
regular  course  of business  and in accordance  with  generally  accepted  accounting  principles,  and
not created and maintained  for tax purposes.  A service  supplier  has the burden to prove the proper
valuation  of the taxable  and nontaxable  services.

  periods  than another,  the duty  to collect  shall  arise separately  for each billing  period.

  the hearing,  the tax administrator  or his or her designee  shall  issue a final  assessment
  confirming,  modifying  or rejecting  the original  deficiency  determination,  and shall mail a
  copy  of such final  assessment  to the person  owing  the tax. The  decision  of the tax
  administrator  may be appealed  pursuant  to Section  7.29.170  of this chapter.  A hearing
  request to the tax administrator  and appeal to the city council  pursuant  to Section  7.29.170

deposited  and paid  into the general  fund  of the city  and expended  for any lawful  purpose  of the
city  as the city council  may determine.

No  injunction,  writ  of mandate,  or other  legal  or equitable  process  shall  issue in any suit,  action,
or proceeding  in any court  against  this city or against  any employee  or officer  of the city to prevent
or enjoin  the collection  under  this chapter  of any tax or any amount  of tax required  to be collected
and/or  remitted.

Section  7.29.200  Remedies  Cumulative

All  remedies  and penalties  prescribed  by this  chapter  or which  are available  under  any  other
provision  of law or equity  are cumulative.  The use of one or more  remedies  by the city  shall  not
bar the use of any other remedy  forthe  purpose  of enforcing  the provisions  of this chapter  provided
only  that the city  may not collect  any liability  under  this chapter  more  than once.

Section  7.29.210  Notice  of Changes  to Ordinance

If a tax under  this chapter  is added,  repealed,  increased,  reduced,  or the tax base is changed,  the
tax  administrator  shall  provide  notice  as Public  Utilities  Code  Section  799  requires.  Before
effective  date of the ordinance  change,  each service  supplier  shall  provide  the tax administrator
with  a copy  of any written  procedures  describing  the information  the service  supplier  needs  to
implement  the ordinance  change.  If the service  supplier  fails  to provide  such written  instructions,
the tax administrator,  or his or her agent,  shall  send, by first  class mail,  a copy  of the ordinance
change  to all collectors  and remitters  of the city's  utility  users taxes according  to the latest payment
records  of the tax administrator.

obligations effectively and consistently.

submitted  by the contractor  until  the month  of March  31, 2026.

permeable  pavers,  park  benches  and picnic  tables,  safety  lighting,  and  other  park  amenities

  PURPOSE:  To  consider  amending  agreement  number  2022-116-CC  Avant-Garde,  Inc.,  to
  provide  continued  assistance  in administering  the Community  Development  Block  Grant  (CDBG)
  and HOME  Investment  Partnership  (HOME)  Programs.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Amendment  No. 1 to Contract  No. 2022-116-CC  with  Avant-Garde,  Inc.,  for
  as needed  administrative  services  for the CDBG  and HOME  Programs  ("Agreement")  as
  follows:
  a.  A six-month  extension  from  January  1, 2026,  through  June 30, 2026, to align  the
  contract  with  the City's  fiscal  year, in an amount  not to exceed  $110,000,  and
  b.  A one-year  term  from  July  1, 2026,  through  June 30, 2027,  in an amount  not to
  exceed  $221,000.
  b.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the Agreement,  in  a form  acceptable  to the  City
  Attorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  Funding  for these administrative  services  will  come  from  the City's  annual
  CDBG  and HOME  allocations.  The contract  does not obligate  the City  to expend  the full  amount
  if Avant  Garde's  services  are no longer  required.  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.

  ANALYSIS:  The Community  Development  Department's  Housing  Division  manages  the CDBG,
  HOME,  and  HOME-ARP  Programs  :tunded  by the  U.S.  Department  of Housing  and  Urban
  Development  (HUD),  as well  as the South  Gate Housing  Authority's  Housing  Choice  Voucher
  (HCV),  Emergency  Housing  Voucher  (EHV),  and Foster  Youth  to Independence  (FYI)  Programs.
  Additionally,  the Division  oversees  the CalHome  Mortgage  Assistance  Program,  Permanent  Local
  Housing  Allocation  (PLHA)  Program,  and Successor  Agency  to the Redevelopment  Agency.

  With  only  four  fiill-time  employees,  the continuation  of housing  consulting  services  is critical  to
  ensure timely  delivery  of services  to low-income  residents  and compliance  with  HUD  deadlines.

 SUBJECT:  AGREEMENT  FOR  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  WITH  SOUTHSTAR
 ENGINEERING  &  CONSULTING,  INC.  FOR  ON-CALL  TECHNICAL  ADVISORY
 SUPPORT  FOR  THE  LACMTA  SOUTHEAST  GATEWAY  LINE  PROJECT

 PURPOSE:  The  Southeast  Gateway  Line  (SGL)  is  a multibillion-dollar  project  being
 advanced  by Metro  in collaboration  with  the Gateway  Cities  Council  of Government  (COG)  and
 its member  cities.  Because  the project  affects  the City's  transportation  infrastructure  as well  as
 other  private  rights-of-way,  Metro  is  soliciting  cornrnents  from  the  Cities.  The  City  is
 recommending  assistance  from  Southstar  Engineering  to meet  the  technical  demands  of the
 project.

 RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Professional  Services  Agreement  with  Southstar  Engineering  & Consulting,
  Inc. to provide  on-call  technical  advisory  support  for the LACTMA  Southeast  Gateway
  Line  Project,  for  not to exceed  amount  of Forty-Nine  Thousand  Eight  Hundred  Sixty
  Dollars  ($49,860);
  b.  Appropriating  $200,000  in  LA  Metro  Regional  Measure  M  Funds  to  the  Southeast
  Gateway  Line  Light  Rail Project  and add it to the Capital  Improvement  Program;
  c.  Authorizing  the City  Manager  to approve  and execute  amendments  up to a cumulative
  amoiu'it  of $50,000;  and
  d.  Authorizing  the  Mayor  to  execute  the  Professional  Services  Agreement  in  a form
  acceptable  to the City  Attorney.

 FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The proposed  Agreement  is in the
 amoiu'it  of $49,860 and will  be funded  with  Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan  Transportation
 Authority  (Metro)  Regional  Measure  M Funds.  In addition,  an appropriation  in the amoiu'it  of
 $200,000 is requested  from  Regional  Measure  M Funds  to establish  the overall  project  budget.
 This  appropriation  will  fund  the  Agreement  as well  as any  additional  related  professional
 services  that  may  be required,  such  as support  from  other  consultants,  staff  time,  and project
 management.

 ANALYSIS:  The Southeast  Gateway  Line  (SGL)  Project  is a multibillion-dollar,  complex,  and
 highly  technical  infrastructure  project  led  by  the  Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan

  209
 Transportation  Authority  (Metro).  Under  the  Master  Cooperative  Agreement  with  Metro,  the
City  is required  to provide  extensive  technical  review  services,  including  detailed  engineering
comments,  project  coordination,  and timely  responses  to Metro's  design  submittals  and requests
for input.

The  scale  and  complexity  of the  SGL  Project  (currently  estimated  at more  than  $8 billion)
significantly  exceed  the  routine  scope  of  work  typically  handled  by  the  City's  Engineering
Division.  The project  involves  multidisciplinary  elements  such as rail  design,  utility  relocations,
roadway  modifications,  structures,  grade separations,  and inter-agency  coordination,  all of which
require  specialized  expertise  and intensive  review  efforts.

At  the  same time,  the Engineering  Division  is actively  managing  more  than  $100  million  in
ongoing  Capital  Improvement  Program  (CIP)  projects  citywide.  In addition,  the Division  has
recently  undergone  restructuring  and now includes  a higher  proportion  of entry-level  engineering
staff  who  are focused  on delivering  the City's  core CIP,  development  review,  and operational
responsibilities.  While  the  Division  remains  :[ully  capable  of  managing  the  City's  capital
program,  it does not have  sufficient  capacity  or specialized  resources  to absorb  the additional
workload  and  technical  demands  of  the  SGL  Project  without  affecting  other  critical  City
priorities.

Further,  the Master  Cooperative  Agreement  requires  the  City  to meet  aggressive  turnaround
times  for  technical  review  and  coordination  to  maintain  Metro's  accelerated  design  and
construction  schedule.  Failure  to meet these timelines  could  delay  the regional  project  and limit
the City's  ability  to influence  key design  decisions  affecting  local  infrastructure,  utilities,  traffic
operations,  and community  impacts.

For these reasons,  the use of a professional  services  consultant  is necessary  to supplement  City
staff,  provide  specialized  technical  expertise,  and  ensure  the  City  can meet  its  contractual
obligations.  The consultant  will  support  timely,  thorough,  and informed  technical  review  while
allowing  City  staff  to continue  delivering  the City's  active  CIP  and essential  services  without
disruption.

BACKGROUND:  The  Southeast  Gateway  Line  (SGL)  Project  is a multibillion-dollar  transit
project  led by the Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan  Transportation  Authority  (LACMTA  or
Metro),  in collaboration  with  multiple  cities,  including  the City  of South  Gate.  The project  will
construct  a new  light  rail  transit  (LRT)  line  connecting  southeastern  Los  Angeles  County  to
Downtown  Los Angeles.

Within  the Gateway  Cities  subregion,  the project  includes  approximately  14.5 miles  of light  rail,
10 stations,  15 aerial  grade  separations,  30 at-grade  crossings,  and crossings  of three rivers  and
four  freeways.  Based  on the latest  estimates,  Metro  anticipates  total  project  costs to exceed  $8
billion.  Preliminary  construction  activities  have  begun  and  are  currently  focused  on  utility
relocations.  Metro  anticipates  the full  line will  be operational  by 2035.

The proposed  contract  was initially  procured  through  a competitive  Request  for Proposals  (RFP)
process.  On October  27, 2025,  the RFP  was  issued  to the City's  on-call  consultants,  Willdan,

  210
 Interwest, and NV5, as well  as Southstar  Engineering  & Consulting,  Inc.  No  proposals  were
received  by the November  20, 2025,  submittal  deadline.

In accordance  with  the South  Gate Municipal  Code,  when  no proposals  are received  through  a
competitive  solicitation,  the City  is authorized  to procure  services  through  a sole-source  process.
As a result,  staff  contacted  Southstar  Engineering  & Consulting,  Inc.,  which  has demonstrated
relevant  experience  providing  similar  services  to other  cities  on the  same project.  Southstar
Engineering  subsequently  submitted  a proposal,  and staff  recommend  awarding  a Professional
Services  Agreement  in the amount  of $49,860.

Awarding  this contract  will  allow  the City to participate  meaningfully  in the SGL Project  without
jeopardizing  Metro's  accelerated  schedule.  Given  current  staffing  limitations,  Southstar  will
serve as the City's  technical  plan reviewer  and coordination  lead, helping  bridge  the gap between
the City's  available  resources  and the pace and complexity  of the project.

In  addition,  Southstar  will  assist  in  centralizing  and  consolidating  technical  cornrnents  from
Gateway  Cities  Council  of Governments  (GCCOG)  member  cities,  enabling  a coordinated  and
consistent  regional  response  that  protects  shared  interests  and improves  communication  with
Metro.

Southstar  also brings  direct  experience  with  large-scale  infrastructure  projects  delivered  under
alternative  delivery  methods  and accelerated  schedules.  This  experience  positions  the firm  to
effectively  represent  the City's  interests  while  working  collaboratively  with  Metro  to facilitate
timely  reviews,  resolve  technical  issues,  and  support  practical,  mutually  beneficial  project
outcomes.

Project  Understandinq

Southstar understands that the City is seeking assistance to perform and manage constructability
reviews for the Metro's SGL project. This includes a set of plans for grade crossings, station siting
and utility relocations. The City would like Southstar to perform plan reviews as it relates to South
Gate. These will all be handled via Metro's protocol using the Bluebeam pdf software.

To' best serve the City and perform this scope, Southstar  would need the latest plans and
documents;  a list of key City Staff who are knowledgeable of City standards/preferences/desires
(e.g. maintenance  superintendents);  and a few hours of Staff time via virtual meetings;  then
Southstar can, tiandle the rest and generate the comments and return them to LACMTA (see more
details below).

Backgr.ound  Information

The  SGL  Project  is led  by the  Los  Angeles  County  Metropolitan  Transportation  Agency
("LAC!TA",or "Metro"), through various Cities including the City of South Gate. Because, the
project affects- the City's transportation infrastructure as well as other possible private rigtits of
way, Metro is soliciting comments from the cities. It is also important to note that the SGL project
also impacts  a total of 10 of the 28 cities located within the Gateway  Cities Council  of
Governments  (GCCOG) subregion.  The GCCOG helps facilitate and has become a forum for
many discussions  related to the Project.

The SGL Project is a new light rail transit (LRT) that will connect southeastern  Los Angeles (LA)
County to downtown LA. Within the Gateway Cities subregion, the project includes a total of 14.5
miles of light rail, including 10 stations, 15 aerial grade separations, 30 at-grade crossings,  and
will cross 3 rivers and 4 freeways.  LACMTA  estimates their project to cost $7.1B based on
estimates made in 2024 and is currently in the PS&E (Plans, Specifications,  and Estimates) phase
with some early construction  works starting in late 2026 or early 2027. LACMTA forecasts fully
opening the line in 2035.

City  Role with  LACMTA  Project

As LACMTA develops the PS&E for the SGL Project, the plans will naturally  require City review
and approval as the City will issue permits for Metro to construct the Project.  City Staff are often

Important  Factors  to Remember

Southstar wants to highlight important factors for the City's to think about regarding  this entire
plan review process.  Here is a list of our recommendations  in no particular order:

  *  ItisimportantandrecommendedfortheCitytospendthemosttimeandeffortinreviewing
  the plans when they are in the early percentage-level  development  stages rather than the
  later stages.  This is because many of the key geometries  and alignments  are being
  finalized and confirmed at this stage. And at this stage, any requested changes are easier
  to accommodate.  Any changes requested in later stages will likely be met with resistance
  from LACMTA  as that will create an impact to their design schedule.  Some examples
  include:
  o' Adjusting vertical/horizontal  curves for sight distance.
  6 Adjusting contours/grading/slopes  to meet drainage needs, such as ensuring flow
  from public ROW does not enter private property, which may affect structure
  design as well (e.g. retaining walls).
  o 'Adjusting  roadway design to maintain accessibility  to all properties.  Sometimes
  turn movements  or access are reduced due to a design change, which can result
  in complaints  from businesses/residents  Early adjustment  can avoid these
  complaints  or even potential lawsuits.
  o  Influencing  and recommending  landscape treatments  in open space that balance
  maintenance  with aesthetics,  as well as commenting  on types and potential
  placements  of BMP facilities.

  SUBJECT:  PROFESSIONAL  SERVICES  AGREEMENT  WITH  WILLDAN
  ENGINEERING  TO  PROVIDE  AS  NEEDED  PLAN  REVIEW  AND  INSPECTION
  SERVICES  FOR  PUBLIC  WORKS  DEPARTMENT,  FIELD  OPERATIONS  DIVISION

  PURPOSE:  The City's  Capital  Improvement  Program  requires  regular  involvement  from  the
  Field  Operations  Division  to ensure the proper  design  and construction  of infrastructure  systems
  that the Division  ultimately  maintains.  To ensure  appropriate  technical  representation  throughout
  project  delivery,  the  Department  recommends  entering  into  an  agreement  with  Willdan
  Engineering  ("Willdan")  to provide  as-needed  plan  review  and inspection  services  in support  of
  the Public  Works  Department's  Field  Operations  Division.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  a Professional  Services  Agreement  with  Willdan  to provide  as-needed  plan
  check  and inspection  services  in the amount  of  $100,000 annually;  and
  c.  AuthorizingtheMayortoexecutetheAgreementinaformacceptablebytheCityAttorney.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.  The Agreement  will  be fully
  funded  with  restricted  and grant funds  budgeted  in the annual  Capital  Improvement  Program,  for
  a not to exceed  annual  amount  of $100,000.

  ANALYSIS:  The  Public  Works  Department  manages  a  substantial  portfolio  of  capital
  improvement  projects  focused  on critical  infrastructure,  including  streets and sidewalks,  water  and
  sewer systems,  City facilities,  parks,  andtraffic  systems.  The City's  Capital  Improvement  Program
  currently  exceeds  $100  million  and includes  numerous  grant-funded  and regionally  coordinated
  projects  that require  strict  adherence  to schedules,  technical  standards,  and funding  requirements

  Successful  delivery  of these projects  requires  consistent  involvement  from  the Field  Operations
  Division,  which  is responsible  for  long-term  operation  and  maintenance  of  the  completed
  infrastructure.  However,  Field  Operations  staff are primarily  dedicated  to full-time  operational  and
  maintenance  duties,  limiting  their  ability  to participate  fully  in project  delivery  from  design
  through  construction.  In  addition,  the  technical  complexity  and  volume  of  project  plans,
  particularly  for grant-funded  and regional  projects,  require  specialized  expertise  and timely  review
  that exceed  current  staff capacity.

  1

 Limited  involvement  during  the design  and plan  review  phase  can result  in construction-phase
issues,  including  incomplete  improvements,  deviations  from  Field  Operations  standards,  and the
need for change orders to address operational  requirements  identified  after construction  has begun.
These issues can increase  costs, delay project  delivery,  and reduce  overall  project  efficiency.

To address these challenges,  staff recommend  providing  supplemental,  as-needed  plan review  and
inspection  support  dedicated  to the Field  Operations  Division.  This approach  has been successfully
implemented  in the past for the Engineering  Division  and has proven  effective  in strengthening
plan review,  improving  coordination  between  design  and operations,  and reducing  construction-
phase changes.  Providing  similar  support  for Field  Operations  will  ensure  projects  are designed
and constructed  in accordance  with  City  standards  and can be efficiently  operated  and maintained
upon completion.

Accordingly,  staff  recommend  awarding  an agreement  to Willdan  Engineering  for  a three-year
term  in an annual  amount  of $100,000.  The agreement  will  be fully  funded  with  restricted  and
grant fiinds  budgeted  in the Capital  Improvement  Program,  with  no impact  to the General  Fund.

BACKGROTJND:  The Public  Works  Department  is responsible  for managing  local  capital
improvement  projects,  supporting  large  private  development  projects,  and coordinating  regional
infrastructure  initiatives  that  may  impact  or  benefit  the  City.  A  critical  component  of  tis
responsibility  is the timely  and thorough  review  of plans  and specifications  to ensure  technical
accuracy,  compliance  with  City  standards,  constructability,  and  long-term  maintenance
considerations.

Plan review  responsibilities  are shared  among  several  divisions,  including  the Field  Operations
Division.  However,  due to ongoing  operational  and maintenance  demands,  Field  Operations  staff
have  limited  availability  to  consistently  participate  in  project  delivery  from  design  through
construction.  As project  volume  and complexity  have increased,  particularly  for grant-funded  and
regional  projects,  the need for supplemental  technical  support  has become  more pronounced.

To address staffing  capacity  constraints,  the City  previously  issued a Request  for Proposals  (RFP)
for  as-needed  professional  services.  Proposals  were  received  from  several  qualified  firms,
including  Willdan  Engineering,  Interwest,  KOA,  NV5  and SA Associates.  Following  evaluation
and  interviews,  Willdan  was  selected  and  approved  by  City  Council  for  annual  as-needed
professional  services  agreements.

For the proposed  agreement,  staff  requested  proposals  from  the as-needed  services  consultants.
Proposals  were  submitted  by Willdan  only.  After  evaluation,  Willdan  was selected  based on its
demonstrated  organizational  structure  and  ability  to  provide  consistent,  project-wide  Field
Operations  representation.  Willdan  has identified  a qualified  candidate  to be assigned  under  the
proposed  agreement.  This  individual  brings  extensive  experience  in  both  engineering  and
operations  environments,  including  work  with  utility  agencies.  The consultant  will  serve as the
primary  representative  for the Field  Operations  Division  on engineering  projects,  leading  plan
reviews  to ensure  City  standards  and specifications  are consistently  incorporated  and providing
inspection  services  when required.  Field  Operations  staff will  continue  to provide  input  as needed,
while  the consultant  ensures  continuity,  timely  responses,  and effective  coordination  throughout

 the project  lifecycle.

This approach is intended to improve  project outcomes,  minimize  construction-phase  changes, and
ensure the completed infrastructure aligns with Field Operations  requirements,  while allowing  City
staff to remain focused on core operational responsibilities.

SUBJECT:  LOS  ANGELES  COUNTY  DEPARTMENT  OF  PUBLIC  WORKS

PURPOSE:  The City  operates  and maintains  roadway  bridges  through  the services  of the Los
Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Works.  The Council  is requested  to approve  purchase  orders
to perform  maintenance  on two bridges:  Firestone  Blvd  Bridges  spanning  the Rio Hondo  and Los
Angeles  River.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Approving  Purchase  Orders  for the Los Angeles  County  Public  Works  to perform  bridge
  maintenance  services  on various  City  owned  bridges  as a Part of the Bridge  Maintenance
  and Repair,  City  Project  No. 719-ST,  for an amount  not to exceed  $338,480;  and
  b. Appropriating  $200,480  in Proposition  C Funds  to the Bridge  Maintenance  and Repair,
  CIP Project  No. 719-ST.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The total  amount  of the Purchase
Orders  is $338,480  and will  be funded  entirely  with  Proposition  C funds,  including  a proposed
$200,480  appropriation  and $138,000 that is already  budgeted  in the Fiscal  Year 2025/26  Capital
Improvement  Program.

ANALYSIS:  The City  is responsible  for the operation  and maintenance  of City-owned  bridges.
The Los Angeles  County  Department  of Public  Works  ("'County"),  in coordination  with  Caltrans,
conducts  periodic  inspections  of these bridges  and provides  recommended  maintenance  actions
through  formal  Bridge  Inspection  Reports.  The City typically  implements  these recommendations
using  a phased  approach  to ensure that adequate  funding  is available  for necessary  repairs.

To support  this effort,  the City has budgeted  approximately  $470,000 for bridge maintenance over
recent  fiscal  years.  Of  this  amount,  approximately  $138,000 remains available  for required
maintenance  improvements,  as portions  of the work  have been completed  and some funds  have
already  been expended.  The County  has now  provided  cost estimates  totaling  $388,480 for the
remaining  phases of work  proposed  for the Firestone  Boulevard  Bridges  spanning  the Rio Hondo
and Los Angeles  River.  Accordingly,  staff recommends  an additional  appropriation  of $200,480
in Proposition  C :[unds to fully  fund  the service  requests  identified  by the County  to date and to

  PURPOSE:  Constniction of the 9923 San Luis Avenue Parking Lot Improvements ("Project")
  has been completed. The City of South Gate ("City") must formally accept the completion of the
  Project.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City Council  will  consider:
  a.  Accepting completion of construction, effective May 26, 2025, of the 9923 San Luis
  Avenue Parking Lot Improvements, City Project No. 63-SP, constructed by Golden Coast
  Construction Inc.; and

  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

  Reserves. The final construction contract amount is $121,918.

  ANALYSIS:  Construction of the Project was substantially completed on May 26, 2025. There
  were no Stop Notices against the project. As such, based on the Public Contract Code section
  7107, staff released the final payment of the 5% retention held from construction invoice
  payments to Golden Coast Construction since it has been more than 60 days of cessation of work
  on the project.

  BACKGROUND:  The Project is included in the Fiscal Year 2025/26 Capital Improvement
  Program ("CIP"). The project involved reconstructing the existing parking lot to clearly separate
  and delineate private parking from public parking areas. Improvements included  removal  of an
  existing landscaped island, relocation of parking lot lighting, and installation of fencing, signage,
  and striping to ensure the parking areas function properly and are well designed for use by the
  property  owner  and the public.

  On February 11, 2025, the City Council approved Contract No. 2025-13-CC with Golden Coast
  Construction, for the improvement of the 9923 San Luis Ave Parking Lot Improvements,  City
  Project No. 63-SP, in an amount not-to-exceed $105,168. Construction began on April 14, 2025,
  and it was substantially completed on May 26, 2025.

necessary  work.  The record  drawing  showed  an existing  electrical  conduct  that was proposed  to
be used.  The conduit  was not found;  a new  conduit  was installed  at the north  perimeter  of the
parking  lot.

The final  construction  cost was $121,918.

The  contractor  has  successfully  fulfilled  all  contract  obligations,  completing  the  project  in

craftsmanship,  delivered  within  budget,  and  completed  on  schedule.  Final  inspections  have
confirmed  that all improvements  meet the required  standards.

position  to formally  accept  the project  and authorize  the filing  of the Notice  of Completion  with
the Los Angeles  County  Registrar-Recorder's  Office.

  COMPLETION  PHASE,  CITY  PROJECT  N0.  539-PRK.

  PURPOSE:  Construction  of the Urban  Orchard  Park  Project  ("Project")  has been  completed.
  The City  of South  Gate ("City")  must formally  accept the completion  of the Project.

  RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  The City  Council  will  consider:
  a.  Accepting  completion  of construction,  effective  October  16, 2025,  of the Urban  Orchard
  Completion  Phase,  City  Project  No.  539-PRK,  constructed  by Los Angeles  Engineering,
  Inc; and
  b.  Approving  Contract  Change  Order  in the amount  of $323,789  to fiu'id Measure  W;
  c.  Appropriating  $1,100,342  from  to  San  Gabriel  and  Lower  Los  Angeles  Rivers  sand
  Mountain  Conservancy  Grant  to the Urban  Orchard  Completion  Phase, City  Project  No.
  539-PRK;
  d. Appropriating  $285,000 from the Los Angeles Coiu'ity  Regional  Park  and Open  Space
  District- Measure  A Technical  Assistance Program  Grant  to  the  Urban  Orchard
  Completion  Phase, City  Project  No. 539-PRK;  and
  e.  Directing  the City  Clerk  to file  a Notice  of Completion  with  the Los  Angeles  County
  Registrar  Recorder's  Office.

  FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no impact  to the General  Fund.  The  final  construction  contract
  amount  is  $6,953,303, inclusive  of the original  contract  and approved  change  orders,  and was
  fully  funded  with  grant funds  and local  return  funds.

  ANALYSIS:  Construction of the Pro5ect was completed on October 16, 2025. No Stop Notices
  were filed  against  the Project.  Accordingly,  pursuant  to Public  Contract  Code Section  7107,  staff
  released  the  final  payment,  including  the  remaining  5 percent  retention  withheld  from
  construction  progress  payments  to Los Angeles  Engineering,  as more  than 60 days have elapsed
  since cessation  of work  on the Project.

  BACKGROUND:  The Project  is included  in the Fiscal  Year 2025/26  Capital  Improvement
  Program  ("CIP")  and has been :[ully  constructed  and is now open for public  use. The Project
  delivered  a new passive  park along the Los Angeles  River  that integrates  stormwater  capture  and
  treatment  features  with  recreational  and educational  amenities.  The approximately  7-acre  site,

  1
  255
 located  at 9475 W. Frontage  Road,  provides  a functional  open space that supports  environmental
education,  active  and passive  recreation,  and improved  stormwater  management,  consistent  with
the City's  sustainability  and river-adjacent  enhancement  goals. The Project  enhances  public
access to open space, promotes  community  health  and environmental  awareness,  and provides
residents  with  new recreational  and educational  opportunities  along the Los Angeles  River.

On November  11, 2024,  the City  Council  approved  Contract  No. 2024-91-CC  with  Los Angeles
Engineering  Inc. for the construction  of the Urban  Orchard  Park Completion  Phase, City  Project
No.  539-PRK,  in an amount  not-to-exceed  $6,546,592.  Construction  began  on November  27,
2024,  and it was completed  on October  16, 2025.

Contract  Change  Order  No.  1, in the  amount  of  $82,922,  was  approved  administratively  to
address  necessary  construction  adjustments  and  closeout  items  identified  during  park
construction.  The  change  order  included  correcting  project  cost  allocations,  adjusting  the
alignment  of underground  water  pipelines,  performing  required  soil remediation,  raising  utility
vaults  to  final  grade,  integrating  radio  equipment  to  communicate  with  the  City's  existing
SCADA  system,  accounting  for inclement  weather  delays,  and reconciling  items  that resulted  in
no net cost change.

Contract  Change  Order  No.  2, in the amount  of $323,789,  was issued  to complete  additional
required  work  to ensure  the park  was fully  functional,  compliant,  and safe for public  use. This
work  iricluded  procurement  of  missing  pump  station  components,  minor  revisions  to  the
playground  layout,  protection  of  electrical  conduits,  extension  of  electrical  infrastructure,
placement  of protective  boulders  over  underground  electrical  boxes,  adjustments  to wetland
monitoring  equipment,  installation  of outreach  and educational  banners,  additional  playground
surfacing  to meet  ADA  requirements,  irrigation  system  improvements  and repairs,  fabrication
and installation  of new entrance  gate arms,  installation  of a surnp pump,  and final  reconciliation
of construction  quantities.

The final  construction  cost of Urban  Orchard  Park Completion  Phase was $6,953,303.

The  contractor  has  successfully  fulfilled  all  contract  obligations,  completing  the  project  in
accordance  with  the approved  plans  and specifications.  The work  was performed  with  quality
cra'Jtsmanship,  delivered  within  budget,  and  completed  on  schedule.  Final  inspections  have
confirmed  that all improvements  meet the required  standards.

With  the project  now  complete  and all contract  requirements  satisfied,  the City  Council  is in a
position  to formally  accept  the project  and authorize  the filing  of the Notice  of Completion  with
the Los Angeles  County  Registrar-Recorder's  Office.

minutes_text:
CITY OF SOUTH GATE
  REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  MINUTES
  TUESDAY, JANUARY 27, 2026

CALL TO ORDER  Joshua Barron, Mayor called a Regular City Council Meeting to order at
  6:31 p.m.

INVOCATION  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation
PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE  Manuel Arana, Chief of Police

ROLL CALL  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk

PRESENT  Mayor Joshua Barron, Vice Mayor Al Rios, Council Member Maria del
  Pilar Avalos, Council Member Maria Davila and Council Member Gil
  Hurtado; City Treasurer Jose De La Paz, City Manager Rob Houston, City
  Attorney Raúl F. Salinas

DEVIATE FROM
THE AGENDA  Mayor Barron requested that the portion of the Comments from the
  Audience - Non-Agenda Items regarding ICE be moved up in the agenda
  to accommodate speakers. Council Member Avalos seconded Mayor
  Barron’s motion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Yancy Lopez, South Gate business owner spoke about an assault by an
  unidentified border patrol or ICE agent inside of her business on Thursday,
  January 22nd. She feels unsafe and unprotected and inquired about the
  Council’s power to protect South Gate residents.

  Caroline, South Gate resident, questioned Council’s lack of participation
  against ICE agents. She is also disappointed with the South Gate residents.
  She will be posting on social media about taxes that won’t be helping
  residents.

  Jimmy Ozaeta, South Gate resident, stated residents are looking to Council
  for help but instead receive silence. He read on social media Mayor
  Barron’s statement against ICE enforcement activities, but residents need
  action not statements.
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT’D  Elia Dominguez Ozaeta stated Council needs to walk around the city
  showing residents, they have Council’s support and the Chief’s protect &
  serve.

  Lizette also questioned Council’s lack of participation during the
  protesting.

  Liz Ruiz, Kauffman Avenue, is concerned about the incidents in
  Minneapolis. She feels that saying Council haven’t done anything is
  unfair. She has seen Council Members Barron, Hurtado and Davila attend
  two protests in South Gate. She has sent articles to Council on what other
  cities are doing.

  Nelson Hermosillo, Dorothy Avenue, stated he is 100% against U.S.
  Border Patrol being anywhere near inner cities. He is 100% in favor of
  meaningful immigration reform, meaning amnesty. He is not blaming
  Council nor defending them. He is going to hold everyone present
  accountable and mentioned googling the Dignity Act. He suggested calling
  the representatives and holding them accountable.

  Huntington Park resident and stakeholder stated the community are very
  involved and her Councilmembers are very present. She suggested
  working with SELA.

EMAILS  Patty suggested meetings be held VIA Zoom to increase participation from
  student parents that are concerned about ICE activities in the community.

  Mayor Barron stated they are not allowed to talk about policy or bring up
  any decisions regarding this.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, stated the city is actively involved in
  litigation against the Department of Justice (DOJ). The city is one of
  twenty-two (22) other cities that have joined forces against the DOJ. The
  cities are involved in a pending litigation right now against Homeland
  Security, ICE, and the DOJ. The lawsuit is called PERDOMO. City
  Attorney Salinas stated many speakers’ attending tonight’s meeting might
  be called as witnesses.

  Mayor Barron spoke how Council is active during these concerned times.

  Chief of Police Arana stated seeing fear and pain many in the community
  are feeling right now. He too came to this country from another country.
  Everyone’s concerns are valid and matters to him and to the police
  department. He mentioned the California Values Act and Truth Act that
  limits the role of local law enforcement regarding issues of immigration.

  Page 2 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT’D  Councilmember Avalos spoke regarding community concerns related to
  safety and trust with law enforcement, particularly in situations involving
  victims of assault and the importance of properly documenting incidents
  through police reports. She requested clarification on City policies and
  protocols to ensure victims can obtain police reports for use in legal
  proceedings. She also expressed concern about fear within the community
  related to immigration enforcement activity and emphasized the
  importance of ensuring residents feel safe and informed about their rights,
  noting her outreach efforts are conducted directly and not shared on social
  media for safety reasons.

  Chief of Police Arana stated people may come into the Police Department
  and file a report. Depending on the situation, the department determines if
  it’s a crime or something that needs to be documented for legal purposes
  other than a crime.

  Vice Mayor Rios seems federal agencies have no regard for the rights of
  individuals.

  Councilmember Hurtado stated even his wife is afraid to speak Spanish.
  He has noticed the low participation from the public to JAA, South Gate
  Aquatics, AYSO and all the other organizations are facing the same
  challenges due to fear of going out.

  Councilmember Davila thanked everyone that spoke tonight. She too is an
  immigrant and stated Council participates in different ways to help the
  community. She suggested the community call the congresswoman.

  Mayor Barron stated if anyone needs resources for food, please call
  Southeast Leadership Network at (323) 804-6639. He asked Jimmy
  Ozaeta, who works for YMCA, to speak about resources.

  Jimmy Ozaeta suggested seeking help from local YMCA, Southeast Real
  YMCA in Maywood or at YMCALA.ORG.

  Councilmember Avalos directed staff to post those resources on the city’s
  website.

  City Manager Houston will check the city’s website. The list is extensive
  on the LA resource line.

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 7:23 p.m., and reconvened at 7:32 p.m., with
  all Members of Council present.

  Page 3 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

1
BUDGET ADMIN/
ELECTION ADMIN  The City Council considered receiving and filing a presentation on South
  Gate's Budget Status and the Components Required to be Completed to
  Design a Utility Users Tax Measure.

  a. Adopting a Resolution declaring a Fiscal Emergency;

  b. Adopting a Resolution calling a Special Election, request that the Los
  Angeles County Board of Supervisors ("Board of Supervisors")
  authorize the Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder / County Clerk
  ("County Elections Official") to render all services necessary to
  conduct the Election, allow for Ballot Arguments, and an Impartial
  Analysis; and

  c. Reviewing the draft Ordinance for voter consideration of the Utility
  Users Tax.

  d. Presentation from Council Meeting of January 13, 2026.

  Item 1 was unanimously continued to the Regular City Council Meeting of
  February 24, 2026, by motion of Council Member Hurtado and seconded
  by Council Member Avalos.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes; Council Member Davila, yes; Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron,
  yes.

RECESS  The City Council recessed at 10:33 p.m., and reconvened at 10:42 p.m.,
  with all Members of Council present.

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS  Robyn Logan, Hunt Avenue, stated that back in December she brought up
  the topic of safety and pedestrians. On Saturday she was almost hit near
  Tweedy and Alexander. She was almost hit yesterday at Hildreth and
  Tweedy on the crosswalk. She questioned what Council is going to do to
  keep residents safe. The chief can only do so much due to being
  understaff.

  Nelson Hermosillo, Dorothy Avenue, invited Council to sit on the pews
  when having lengthy speeches. He is 100% opposed to Border Patrol
  operating not only in South Gate, but also in surrounding cities. What’s
  happening in Minneapolis is coming back to California. He doesn’t agree
  with Council adjourning the City Council Meetings in memory of those
  individuals because it can give some individuals the wrong message to
  interfere with federal operations. He believes in rule law, respect law

  Page 4 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT’D  enforcement officers and hold them accountable. He asked Council if
  those exact circumstances would have happened with a police officer
  shooting, would Council adjourn in memory of that individual that lost
  his/her life.

  Liz Ruiz, Kauffman Avenue, thanked Council for adjourning the meetings
  in memory of the individuals. It shows Council standing with the
  community and their civil rights. She mentioned an incident with the trash
  company.

  South Gate resident, spoke on behalf of a resident that resides at 2647
  Kansas Avenue stating streetlights have been out. She informed that
  resident about the app. She is also disappointed because people spoke
  about ICE in the beginning and now everyone has left.

EMAILS  Circle Park resident noted orders from GWS composting facility on Miller
  Way have decreased but expressed skepticism that the improvement will
  be permanent based on the company’s past practices.

  Mario Dominguez requested a timeline for the start of the completion of
  the fiber optic cable project and will construction impact Tweedy
  Boulevard due to its recent pavement and new city branding. He also
  criticized the project for not improving the city council chambers network
  or live stream capabilities and questioned the overall benefit of the project
  to residents.

  Mayor Barron asked if anyone could reply to tonight’s comments.

  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, stated with regards to the
  concerns for pedestrian safety on Tweedy and particularly at Pinehurst,
  phase II of the Tweedy Mile Complete Street Project will be starting
  construction soon. The city is waiting for approval from Cal Trans for
  funding and then bid the project. The city is making pedestrian crossing
  improvements on Tweedy. With regards to the trash company, feel free to
  contact the public works department and the city can facilitate service. As
  to the lights on Kansas and fiber optic project that construction started
  yesterday. The construction will take place for 8 weeks. It will occur on
  California from our south city limit to our north city limit. It is going to
  connect the city hall, and it is not going to impact the pavement on
  Tweedy Mile.

  Mayor Barron asked the Chief of Police if he would like to add anything
  to Ms. Logan’s comments regarding public safety on Tweedy.

  Page 5 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

COMMENTS FROM THE
AUDIENCE - NON-AGENDA
ITEMS CONT’D  Chief of Police Arana stated traffic safety is a major concern for the police
  department. The chief has redirected some of the personnel towards traffic
  to improve our presence and enforcement. They have put on social media
  information regarding traffic and have increased citations. The goal is not
  to go out and site everyone. The goal is to get people to be responsible.

  Mayor Barron knows the state recently passed some laws that may be able
  to help and understands there’s a cost to maintain speeding cameras.

  Vice Mayor Rios stated especially if it’s going to generate revenue.

  Mayor Barron stated most cities say it will not generate revenue because
  of the maintenance.

  Council Member Avalos stated driving up and down on Tweedy,
  specifically on Alexander and twice, she has almost hit a bicyclist who is
  coming the wrong way and one right in the middle and wearing all black.
  She hopes that it can be addressed too.

  Mayor Barron stands on the adjourning in the memory of Alex Pretti given
  his time to serve our veterans as a VA nurse in the ICU.

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Arturo Cervantes, Director of Public Works, nothing to report.

  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation, stated that on
  Thursday there will be a glow-in-the-dark pick ball game at the Sports
  Center.

  Gabe Perez, Director of Community Development, stated a new proposed
  food establishment with drive-through on Firestone Boulevard and Vossler
  Avenue, but tenants are unknown at this time. That at the Council Meeting
  of February 24th Council will receive a report.

  Mr. Perez also reported that the Community Development Department
  obtained $300,000 from Gateway COG to be able to support and finish
  our Gateway District Specific Plan efforts. This is where the Southeast
  Gateway line is going to have a rail station. He mentioned an open house
  on Wednesday, February 18th in the civil center at 6:00 p.m., and it’s open
  to the public to get ideas.

  Luis Fausto, Director of Administrative Services, stated the department is
  experiencing technical issues with the utility payment web portal. This is
  an old system that is no longer supported by the vendor. The department is
  exploring options, fixing or replacing the system.

  Page 6 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS
CONT’D  Mayor Barron asked if any discussion has been had with banking
  institution regarding their ACH systems that customers would like
  automatic bill pay.

  Mr. Fausto stated the city is approving ACH payments for water accounts
  if they are requested. The department is also in the preliminary phase of
  exploring partnerships with grocery stores and other outlets so that they
  can possibly take utility payments on our behalf.

  Jon Hamilton, Director of Human Resources, nothing to report.

  Manny Arana, Chief of Police, nothing to report.

  Rob Houston, City Manager, nothing to report.

  Raúl F. Salinas, City Attorney, nothing to report.

  Jose De La Paz, City Treasurer, nothing to report.

  Yodit Glaze, City Clerk, nothing to report.

  Councilmember Davila, nothing to report.

  Councilmember Hurtado, nothing to report.

  Councilmember Avalos, nothing to report.

  Vice Mayor Rios brought up the issue of the libraries at the last council
  meeting and asked if a room at the park would be available for students to
  study.

  Tina De La Rosa, Acting Director of Parks & Recreation, replied that
  spaces are limited due to scheduled programs.

  Vice Mayor Rios stated maybe LAUSD could be considered because they
  have a lot of facilities.

  Councilmember Davila stated a meeting with LAUSD on Monday,
  February 2nd. Maybe this can be brought up.

  Vice Mayor Rios asked if the city has received reports from the
  organizations receiving money from the city about how many people were
  served due to Mental Health.

  Vice Mayor Rios asked if the council will be receiving a report regarding
  zoom or call-in feature by July 1st.

  Page 7 of 12
   REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES OF JANUARY 27, 2026

REPORTS AND COMMENTS
FROM CITY OFFICIALS  Councilmember Davila asked if council could receive an update when the
  county is planning to open the library.
  Mayor Barron was informed that the library was to open at the end of
  February, but there were additional delays, so it is looking by mid-March.

  Mayor Barron likes the idea of reaching out to LAUSD, regarding their
  school libraries for students.

  Mayor Barron stated that tomorrow he will be at Career Day at St. Helen.
  He will also be at LA County Sanitation orientation taking the grand tour
  of the facility and thereafter the meeting. He mentioned SELA Kiwanis’
  first meeting of the year is tomorrow. He is currently the treasure, no
  longer the president.

CONSENT CALENDAR  Agenda Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, and 9 were approved by motion of Mayor
  Barron and seconded by Vice Mayor Rios. Items 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9 and
  10(a) were pulled for separate discussion.

  ROLL CALL: Council Member Avalos, yes; Council Member Hurtado,
  yes (recused on items 3 and 9); Council Member Davila, yes (recused on
  item 8); Vice Mayor Rios, yes; Mayor Barron, yes.
